summary: The narrator recounts getting in trouble in fifth grade after a PowerPoint on Henry Hastings Sibley, the first governor of Minnesota, whom the narrator portrays as a villain who tricked the Dakota and condemned many of them to death. Sibley, a classmate, and a friend named Dakota objected, and the school psychologist told the narrator to stop being so confrontational. The narrator then describes planning revenge against three girls who had bullied them, starting with fake Snapchat and Kik accounts posing as a cute boy to turn the girls against each other, and picking a weakness for each of them.
one_line: A narrator recounts a fifth-grade Sibley PowerPoint dispute and a later revenge scheme using fake social media accounts against three bullying girls.
key_facts: The narrator's fifth-grade class had to do PowerPoints about Minnesota history, and the narrator's was about Henry Hastings Sibley, the first governor of Minnesota.
Sibley got the Dakota to sign a document they thought was a copy of a treaty, but it was actually a trick to take away their money.
The teacher accused the narrator of making up the story about the treaty trick until the narrator showed her it was in a book that has footnotes.
When Sibley was in charge of the trial after the Dakota war, he got 300 Indians condemned to death.
Only 38 of the condemned Dakota were hanged because Lincoln said it was too many.
The narrator says Sibley is treated like a hero and has counties and high schools named after him.
Sibley the girl, a classmate, had made fun of the narrator on a regular basis in fifth grade.
A classmate named Dakota, who was not the least bit Indian, was also upset about the PowerPoint.
The narrator said "This is about race, you idiots," and was sent to the school psychologist, who said they had to stop being so confrontational.
The narrator created fake Snapchat and Kik accounts for a boy who was cute and cool, and chatted privately with each of the three girls.
The narrator used things the girls said about each other to drive a wedge between them.
Lyndsay also sent embarrassing naked selfies to the fake account.
For Rebecca, the narrator picked her hair as the weapon, since she constantly played with it and freaked out over split ends.
Harper was described as the tough, meanest one of the three girls.
The narrator says what happened to Sibley later happens to kids all the time, but nobody does anything about it.
